claim: Let \(p,q\) be distinct primes, \(a,b\ge1\), \(N=(a+1)(b+1)\), and \(X\) any set of \(N\) distinct integers. Write \(T=\#\{x\in X:pq\mid x\}\), \(B=\#\{x\in X:p\mid x,\ q\nmid x\}\), \(C=\#\{x\in X:q\mid x,\ p\nmid x\}\), \(R=N-T-B-C\), and \(F_u(k)=u!/(u-k)!\) for \(0\le k\le u\), zero otherwise. The exact number \(M\) of bijections \(X\to D(p^a q^b)\) having every paired gcd equal to one is: \(M=0\) if \(T\ge2\); \(M=F_b(B)F_a(C)R!\) if \(T=1\); \(M=[F_b(B)F_a(C)+B F_b(B-1)F_a(C)+C F_a(C-1)F_b(B)](N-B-C)!\) if \(T=0\). For \(T=0\) a matching exists exactly when \(B\le b+1\), \(C\le a+1\), not simultaneously \(B=b+1,C=a+1\); for \(T=1\) exactly when \(B\le b,C\le a\). For \(n=225\), progressions \(X=\{1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17\}\) and \(Y=\{1,5,9,13,17,21,25,29,33\}\) have the same counts of multiples of \(3\) and \(5\), namely \((3,2)\), but yield \(480\) and \(288\) matchings.

integrity.claim_scope: Complete exact counting theorem with proof and finite independent program checks

scientific_limitations: Exactly two distinct prime factors; X must contain (a+1)(b+1) distinct integers. Earlier generalized permanent evaluations may have priority. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove universal formula.
title: Exact coprime-matching multiplicities for two-prime-power divisor sets
